This body which is seated in the palanquin is known as "thou" thence what is elsewhere called this is here distinguished as thou and I. I and thou and others are made of elements and elements, influenced by qualities, assume a bodily shape. Qualities depend on acts, and acts perpetrated in ignorance influence the condition of all beings. The soul is pure, imperishable, tranquil, devoid of qualities, distinct from nature and is without increase or diminution; and if it is freed from increase or diminution then with what prosperity you say to me, ‘I see that you are robust? If the palanquin is placed on the body, the body on the feet, the feet the ground, then the burden is carried as much by you as by me. Why are not others, O king, feeling the burden of this palanquin. If I am exhausted with a burden that is being carried on another's shoulder, then why with the weight of this palanquin, people may be worn out with the weight of mountains, trees, houses and even of the earth, When the nature of men is different, either in its essence or its cause, then it may be said that fatigue is to be undergone by me. The material, with which the palanquin is made, is the substance of you and me and of all others being a collection of Elements collected by individuality.'

Parāçara said:—Having said this the Brahman became silent and went on carrying the palanquin; the king too speedily got down from it and touched his feet. The king said: O Brahman, leave off the palanquin and be propitiated with me. Tell me who art thou under the disguise of a fool? The Brahman replied "Hear me, king. Who I am it is not possible to say; I go anywhere for receiving the fruits of good and bad luck. The body is produced for the enjoyment of pleasure and endurance of pain. Pleasure and pain originate from virtue and vice; therefore the soul assumes bodily shape for enjoying pleasure and enduring pain consequent upon virtue and vice. The universal cause of all living creatures is virtue or vice, why therefore enquire after the cause of my coming to this earth."

The king said:—"That virtue and vice are the causes of all actions and that people migrate into various bodies for receiving their consequences, there is not the least doubt about it; but as regards what you have said that it is not possible for you to say who you are, it is a matter which I wish to have explained. O Brahman, how cannot a man declare himself to be that which he (really) is: there can be no harm to one's self from applying to it the word 'I'".

The Brahmana said:—"To use the word ‘I' undoubtedly is detrimental; but it is not improperly used if it is applied merely to the soul. But the term is erroneous in as much as it conceives that to be the self or soul which is not self or soul. The tongue articulates the word ‘I' assisted by the lips, the teeth and the palate; and these are the origin of the expression, as they are the causes of the production of speech.

"If by these instruments speech can utter the word 'I' it is not at all proper to say that speech itself is ‘I.' O king, the body of a man having hands, feet and other limbs is composed of various parts: to what part shall we apply the word ‘I'? If another being had existed in this body quite different from me, then it may be said, O king, that this is I, that is the other; while one soul inhabits the whole body, then such questions as 'Who are you? Who am I?' are useless. Thou art a monarch; this is a palanquin: these are the bearers: these are thy followers; yet it is untrue that these are thine. This palanquin, in which thou art seated, is made of timber got from trees. Then tell me, what name, tree, timber or palanquin, shall be applied to it, O king. The people shall not say that their monarch is seated on a tree or on a timber but they shall say that he is in the palanquin. The artificial assemblage of the pieces of timber is called the palanquin: judge yourself, therefore, O king, in what the palanquin differs from the wood. Again consider the sticks of the umbrella, in their separate state. What then is the umbrella? Apply this argument to thee and to me. A man, a woman, a cow, a goat, a horse, an elephant, a bird, a tree, are names given to various bodies, which they assume on account of their primitive actions. Man is neither a god, nor a man, nor a beast, nor a tree: these are the various shapes which he assumes on account of his acts. O king, your name is Vasuraja and another name is Rajabhat—besides you have got various other names—but none of these names is real and is nothing but the work of imagination. And what thing is there in the world, O king, which being subject to changes, does not in the course of time, go by different names? You are called the king of the world, the son of your father, the enemy of your foes, the husband of your wife, the father of your children, what name the shall I apply to you? What is your situation? Are you the head or the belly? Or are they yours? Are you the feet or are they yours? You are, O king, separate in nature from the members of your body. Then considering properly, do you think who I am. And since the truth has been got at, how is it possible for me to recognize the distinction and to apply to my individual the expression 'I'".

verses.sa:
श्रीपराशर उवाच
निशम्य तस्येति वचः परमार्थसमन्वितम् ।
प्रश्रयावनतो भूत्वा तमाह नृपतिर्द्विजम् ॥
verses.rom:
shriparashara uvacha
nishamya tasyeti vachah paramarthasamanvitam |
prashrayavanato bhutva tamaha nripatirdvijam ||

verses.sa:
राजोवाच
भगवन्यत्त्वया प्रोक्तं परमार्थमयं वचः ।
श्रुते तस्मिन्भ्रमन्तीव मनसो मम वृत्तयः ॥
verses.rom:
rajovacha
bhagavanyattvaya proktam paramarthamayam vachah |
shrute tasminbhramantiva manaso mama vrittayah ||

verses.sa:
एतद्विवेकविज्ञानं यदशेषेषु जन्तुषु ।
भवता दर्शितं विप्र तत्परं प्रकृतेर्महत् ॥
verses.rom:
etadvivekavijnanam yadashesheshu jantushu |
bhavata darshitam vipra tatparam prakritermahat ||

verses.sa:
नाहं वहामि शिबिकां शिबिका न मयि स्थिता ।
शरीरमन्यदस्मत्तो येनेयं शिबिका धृता ॥
verses.rom:
naham vahami shibikam shibika na mayi sthita |
shariramanyadasmatto yeneyam shibika dhrita ||

verses.sa:
गुणप्रवृत्त्या भूतानां प्रवृत्तिः कर्मचोदिता ।
प्रवर्तन्ते गुणा ह्येते किं ममेति त्वयोदितम् ॥
verses.rom:
gunapravrittya bhutanam pravrittih karmachodita |
pravartante guna hyete kim mameti tvayoditam ||

verses.sa:
एतस्मिन्परमार्थज्ञ मम श्रोत्रपथं गते ।
मनो विह्वलतामेति परमार्थार्थितां गतम् ॥
verses.rom:
etasminparamarthajna mama shrotrapatham gate |
mano vihvalatameti paramartharthitam gatam ||

verses.sa:
पूर्वमेव महाभागं कपिलर्षिमहं द्विज ।
प्रष्टुमभ्युद्यतो गत्वा श्रेयः किं त्वत्र शंस मे ॥
verses.rom:
purvameva mahabhagam kapilarshimaham dvija |
prashtumabhyudyato gatva shreyah kim tvatra shamsa me ||

verses.sa:
तदन्तरे च भवता यदेतद्वाक्यमीरितम् ।
तेनैव परमार्थार्थं त्वयि चेतः प्रधावति ॥
verses.rom:
tadantare cha bhavata yadetadvakyamiritam |
tenaiva paramarthartham tvayi chetah pradhavati ||

verses.sa:
कपिलर्षिर्भगवतः सर्वभूतस्य वै द्विज ।
विष्णोरंशो जगन्मोहनाशायोर्वीमुपागतः ॥
verses.rom:
kapilarshirbhagavatah sarvabhutasya vai dvija |
vishnoramsho jaganmohanashayorvimupagatah ||

verses.sa:
स एव भगवान्नूनमस्माकं हितकाम्यया ।
प्रत्यक्षतामत्र गतो यथैतद्भावतोच्यते ॥
verses.rom:
sa eva bhagavannunamasmakam hitakamyaya |
pratyakshatamatra gato yathaitadbhavatochyate ||

verses.sa:
तन्मह्यं प्रणताय त्वं यच्छ्रेयः परमं द्विजः ।
तद्वदाखिल विज्ञानजलवीच्युदधिर्भवान् ॥
verses.rom:
tanmahyam pranataya tvam yachchhreyah paramam dvijah |
tadvadakhila vijnanajalavichyudadhirbhavan ||

verses.sa:
ब्राह्मण उवाच
भूप पृच्छसि किं श्रेयः परमार्थं नु पृच्छसि ।
श्रेयांस्यपरमार्थानि अशेषाणि च भूपते ॥
verses.rom:
brahmana uvacha
bhupa prichchhasi kim shreyah paramartham nu prichchhasi |
shreyamsyaparamarthani asheshani cha bhupate ||

verses.sa:
देवताराधनं कृत्वा धनसम्पदमिच्छति ।
पुत्रानिच्छति राज्यं च श्रेयस्तस्यैव तन्नृप ॥
verses.rom:
devataradhanam kritva dhanasampadamichchhati |
putranichchhati rajyam cha shreyastasyaiva tannripa ||

verses.sa:
कर्म यज्ञात्मकं श्रेयः फलं तत्प्राप्तिलक्षणम् ।
श्रेयः प्रधानं च फले तदेवानभिसंहिते ॥
verses.rom:
karma yajnatmakam shreyah phalam tatpraptilakshanam |
shreyah pradhanam cha phale tadevanabhisamhite ||

verses.sa:
आत्मा ध्येयः सदा भूप योगयुक्तैस्तथा परम् ।
श्रेयस्तस्यैव संयोगः श्रेयो यः परमात्मनः ॥
verses.rom:
atma dhyeyah sada bhupa yogayuktaistatha param |
shreyastasyaiva samyogah shreyo yah paramatmanah ||

verses.sa:
श्रेयांस्येवमनेकानि शतशोय सहस्रसः ।
सन्त्यत्र परमार्थस्तु न त्वेते श्रूयतां च मे ॥
verses.rom:
shreyamsyevamanekani shatashoya sahasrasah |
santyatra paramarthastu na tvete shruyatam cha me ||

verses.sa:
धर्माय त्यज्यते किन्तु परमार्थो धनं यदि ।
व्ययश्च क्रियते कस्मात्कामप्राप्त्युपलक्षणः ॥
verses.rom:
dharmaya tyajyate kintu paramartho dhanam yadi |
vyayashcha kriyate kasmatkamapraptyupalakshanah ||

verses.sa:
पुत्रश्चेत्परमार्थः स्यात्सोऽप्यन्यस्य नरेश्वर ।
परमार्थभूतः सोन्यस्य परमार्थो हि तत्पिता ॥
verses.rom:
putrashchetparamarthah syatso'pyanyasya nareshvara |
paramarthabhutah sonyasya paramartho hi tatpita ||

verses.sa:
एवं न परमार्थोस्ति जगत्यस्मिञ्चराचरे ।
परमार्थो हि कार्याणि कारणानामशेषतः ॥
verses.rom:
evam na paramarthosti jagatyasmincharachare |
paramartho hi karyani karananamasheshatah ||

verses.sa:
राज्यादिप्राप्तिरत्रोक्ता परमार्थतया यदि ।
परमार्था भवन्त्यत्र न भवन्ति च वै ततः ॥
verses.rom:
rajyadipraptiratrokta paramarthataya yadi |
paramartha bhavantyatra na bhavanti cha vai tatah ||

verses.sa:
ऋग्यजुःसामनिष्पाद्यं यज्ञकर्म मतं तव ।
परमार्थभूतं तत्रापि श्रूयतां गदतो मम ॥
verses.rom:
rigyajuhsamanishpadyam yajnakarma matam tava |
paramarthabhutam tatrapi shruyatam gadato mama ||

verses.sa:
यत्तु निष्पाद्यते कार्यं मृदा कारणभूतया ।
तत्कारणानुगमनाज्ज्ञायते नृप मृण्मयम् ॥
verses.rom:
yattu nishpadyate karyam mrida karanabhutaya |
tatkarananugamanajjnayate nripa mrinmayam ||

verses.sa:
एवं विनाशिभिर्द्रव्यैः समिदाज्यकुशादिभिः ।
निष्पाद्यते क्रिया या तु सा भवित्री विनाशिनी ॥
verses.rom:
evam vinashibhirdravyaih samidajyakushadibhih |
nishpadyate kriya ya tu sa bhavitri vinashini ||

verses.sa:
अनाशो परमार्थश्च प्राज्ञौरभ्युपगम्यते ।
तत्तु नाशि न सन्देहो नाशिद्रव्योपपादितम् ॥
verses.rom:
anasho paramarthashcha prajnaurabhyupagamyate |
tattu nashi na sandeho nashidravyopapaditam ||

verses.sa:
तदेवाफलदं कर्म परमार्थो मतस्तव ।
मुक्तिसाधनभूतत्वात्परमार्थो न साधनम् ॥
verses.rom:
tadevaphaladam karma paramartho matastava |
muktisadhanabhutatvatparamartho na sadhanam ||

verses.sa:
ध्यानं चैवात्मनो भूपु परमार्थार्थशब्दितम् ।
भेदकारि परेभ्यस्तु परमार्थो न भेदवान् ॥
verses.rom:
dhyanam chaivatmano bhupu paramartharthashabditam |
bhedakari parebhyastu paramartho na bhedavan ||

verses.sa:
परमात्मात्मनोर्योगः परमार्थ इतीष्यते ।
मिथ्यैतदन्यद्रव्यं हि नैति तद्द्रव्यतां यतः ॥
verses.rom:
paramatmatmanoryogah paramartha itishyate |
mithyaitadanyadravyam hi naiti taddravyatam yatah ||

verses.sa:
तस्माच्छ्रेयांस्यशेषाणि नृवैतानि न संशयः ।
परमार्थस्तु भूपाल संक्षेपाच्छ्रूयतां मम ॥
verses.rom:
tasmachchhreyamsyasheshani nrivaitani na samshayah |
paramarthastu bhupala samkshepachchhruyatam mama ||

verses.sa:
एको व्यापी समः शुद्धो निर्गुणः प्रकृतेः परः ।
जन्मवृद्ध्यादिरहित आत्मा सर्वगतोव्ययः ॥
verses.rom:
eko vyapi samah shuddho nirgunah prakriteh parah |
janmavriddhyadirahita atma sarvagatovyayah ||

verses.sa:
परज्ञानमयो सद्भिर्नामजात्यादिभिर्विभुः ।
न योगवान्न युक्तोभून्नैव पार्थिव योक्ष्यते ॥
verses.rom:
parajnanamayo sadbhirnamajatyadibhirvibhuh |
na yogavanna yuktobhunnaiva parthiva yokshyate ||

verses.sa:
तस्यात्मपरदेहेषु सतोप्येकमयं हि यत् ।
विज्ञानं परमार्थोऽसौ द्वैतिनोऽतथ्यर्शिनः ॥
verses.rom:
tasyatmaparadeheshu satopyekamayam hi yat |
vijnanam paramartho'sau dvaitino'tathyarshinah ||

verses.sa:
वेणुरन्ध्रप्रभेदेन भेदः षङ्जादिसंज्ञितः ।
अभेदव्यापिनोवायोस्तथास्य परमात्मनः ॥
verses.rom:
venurandhraprabhedena bhedah shanjadisamjnitah |
abhedavyapinovayostathasya paramatmanah ||

verses.sa:
एकस्वरूपभेदश्च ब्राह्मकर्मावृतिप्रजः ।
देवादिभेदेऽपध्वस्ते नास्त्येवावरणे हि सः ॥
verses.rom:
ekasvarupabhedashcha brahmakarmavritiprajah |
devadibhede'padhvaste nastyevavarane hi sah ||

verses.sa: इति श्रीविष्णुमहापुराणे द्वितीयेऽंशे चतुर्दशोऽध्यायः (१४)
verses.rom: iti shrivishnumahapurane dvitiye'mshe chaturdasho'dhyayah (14)

prose.en: Parāçara said:—Having heard his words pregnant with the true essence of things the king humbly said to the twice-born one; "What you have said, O revered sir, is undoubtedly the truth—but in hearing this my mind has been greatly worked up. What you have shown, O twice-born one, in various creatures to be understanding and discriminative knowledge, is very grand and distinct from plastic nature. I have not carried the palanquin nor is it placed on my shoulders. The body, which has carried the palanquin, is different from me. The three qualities influence the actions of the animals and these three qualities are again influenced by destiny. This reaching my ears, O thou conversant with profound truth, my mind has been greatly disturbed for knowing that real and holy truth. O twice-born, I had already addressed myself for going to the great ascetic Kapila, to learn of him what in this life is the most desirable object. But what you have said in the interim has attracted my mind towards you for being acquainted with the profound truth. O Brahmin, the great ascetic Kapila is a portion of the glorious Vishnu, who is at one with all elements. He is born on earth to remove the illusions of the world. But what you have said convinces me that the great Kapala, for my well-being, has appeared within my vision. To me, who am thus asking, O twice-born one, explain what is the best of things, for you are an ocean overflowing with the waters of the divine wisdom". The Brāhmana said—"You ask me, O lord of earth, what is the best of all things, not the great end of life. There are many things which are best in the world and there are many truths of life. O king, some worshipping the gods desire for wealth, prosperity, children or kingdom: these are the best things in their estimation. A sacrifice that gives heavenly pleasures is also the best. That, which gives best rewards though not asked for, is also the best. To him, who with concentration meditates upon the great soul, union with it is the best. Thus there are hundreds and thousands of best things but these are not profound truths. Hear, I shall describe to you what is the profound truth. If wealth is the end of life then why do people spend it for the acquisition of piety and for acquiring desired-for objects? O lord of men, if son is the end of life then the father of that son is another's end of life and he again is another's. If then every action becomes the end of every cause then there exists no supreme or final truth in this world. And if the acquirement of sovereignty be characterized as the great end of life then finite ends would sometimes be and some times cease to be. If you consider the rites laid down by Rik, Yayur and Shāma Vedas as the ends of life, hear what I have got to say on that head. Anything, that is the outcome of the instrumentality of earth, partakes of its character and consists of clay. So any act, that is performed by such perishable things as fuel, clarified butter and Kusha grass, must be in nature perishable. The great end of life must be considered by wise men as eternal and it would be transient if it were accomplished through transitory things. If you consider that which gives no reward to be the true end of life then that which brings on final liberation is not the true end of life. If the union of the individual soul with the Great soul is considered as the supreme end of life then this becomes false: for one substance cannot become substantially another. Thus there are undoubtedly very many best things in this world: hear from me, in short O king, the true end of life. It is soul, one, all-pervading, uniform, perfect supreme over nature, freed from birth, growth and destruction, omnipresent undecaying, made up of true knowledge, independent and not connected with unreal things, with name, species and the rest and in time, present, past and future. The spirit, which is essentially one in one's own and in all other bodies, is the true wisdom of one who knows the unity and the true principles of things. As air spreading all over the world going through the perforation of a flute is distinguished as the notes of the scale so the (true) nature of the great spirit is one though it assumes various forms consequent upon the fruits of actions. When the difference, between the various forms, such as that of god and man, is destroyed then the distinction of things ceases".

verses.sa:
पराशर उवाच ।
इत्युक्ते मौनिनं भूयश्विन्तयानं महीपतिम् ।
प्रत्युवाचाथ विप्रोऽसावदू तौन्तर्गतां कथाम् ॥
verses.rom:
parashara uvacha |
ityukte mauninam bhuyashvintayanam mahipatim |
pratyuvachatha vipro'savadu tauntargatam katham ||

verses.sa:
श्रूयतां नृपशाद्दूल! यदूगोतमृबुणा पुरा ।
अवबोधं जनयता निदाघस्य महात्मनः ॥
verses.rom:
shruyatam nripashaddula! yadugotamribuna pura |
avabodham janayata nidaghasya mahatmanah ||

verses.sa:
ऋभुर्नामाभवत् पुत्रो ब्रह्मणः परमेष्ठिनः ।
विज्ञाततत्त्वसद्रावो निसर्गादेव भूपते ॥
verses.rom:
ribhurnamabhavat putro brahmanah parameshthinah |
vijnatatattvasadravo nisargadeva bhupate ||

verses.sa:
तस्य शिष्यो निदाघोऽबूत् पुलस्त्यतनयः पुरा ।
प्रादादशेषविज्ञानं स तस्मै परया मुदा ॥
verses.rom:
tasya shishyo nidagho'but pulastyatanayah pura |
pradadasheshavijnanam sa tasmai paraya muda ||

verses.sa:
अवाप्यज्ञानत्त्वस्य न तस्यादूतैवासनाम ।
स ऋभुस्तर्कयामास निदाघस्य नरेश्वर ॥
verses.rom:
avapyajnanattvasya na tasyadutaivasanama |
sa ribhustarkayamasa nidaghasya nareshvara ||

verses.sa:
देविकायास्तटे वीरनगरं नाम वै पुरम् ।
समृद्धमतिरम्यं च पुलस्त्येन निवेशितम् ॥
verses.rom:
devikayastate viranagaram nama vai puram |
samriddhamatiramyam cha pulastyena niveshitam ||

verses.sa:
रम्योपवनपर्य्यन्ते स तस्मिन् पार्थिवोत्तम !
निदाघो नाम योगज्ञ ऋभुशिष्योऽवसत् पुरा ॥
verses.rom:
ramyopavanaparyyante sa tasmin parthivottama !
nidagho nama yogajna ribhushishyo'vasat pura ||

verses.sa:
दिव्येवर्षसहस्त्रे तु समतीतेऽस्य तत्पुरम् ।
जगाम स ऋभुः शिष्यं निदाघमवलोककः ॥
verses.rom:
divyevarshasahastre tu samatite'sya tatpuram |
jagama sa ribhuh shishyam nidaghamavalokakah ||

verses.sa:
स तस्य वैश्वदेवान्ते द्रारालोकनगोचरे ।
स्थितस्तेन गृहीतार्घ्यो निजवेश्म प्रवेशितः ॥
verses.rom:
sa tasya vaishvadevante draralokanagochare |
sthitastena grihitarghyo nijaveshma praveshitah ||

verses.sa:
पर्क्षालिताङ घ्रिपाणिं च कृतासनपरिग्रहम् ।
उवाच स द्रिजश्वेष्ठो भूज्यतामिति सादरम् ॥
verses.rom:
parkshalitana ghripanim cha kritasanaparigraham |
uvacha sa drijashveshtho bhujyatamiti sadaram ||

verses.sa:
ऋभुरुवाच ।
भो विप्रवर्य्य! भोक्तव्यं यदन्नं भवतो गृहे ।
तत् कथ्यतां कदन्नेषु न प्रीतिः सतत मम ॥
verses.rom:
ribhuruvacha |
bho vipravaryya! bhoktavyam yadannam bhavato grihe |
tat kathyatam kadanneshu na pritih satata mama ||

verses.sa:
निदाघ उवाच ।
भक्त-यावक-वाठ्यानामपूपानाञ्च मे गृहे ।
यदू रोचते द्रिजश्रेष्ठ!तत् त्वं भुङ श्र्व यथेच्छया ॥
verses.rom:
nidagha uvacha |
bhakta-yavaka-vathyanamapupanancha me grihe |
yadu rochate drijashreshtha!tat tvam bhuna shrva yathechchhaya ||

verses.sa:
ऋभुरुवाच ।
कदन्नानि द्रिजैतानि मृष्टमन्नं प्रयच्छ मे ।
संयाव-पायसादीनि द्रप्स्यफाणितावन्ति च ॥
verses.rom:
ribhuruvacha |
kadannani drijaitani mrishtamannam prayachchha me |
samyava-payasadini drapsyaphanitavanti cha ||

verses.sa:
निदाघ उवाच ।
हे हे शालिनि मदगेहे यत किञ्चिदतिशोभनम् ।
भक्ष्योपसाधनं मष्टं तेनास्यान्नां प्रसाधय ॥
verses.rom:
nidagha uvacha |
he he shalini madagehe yata kinchidatishobhanam |
bhakshyopasadhanam mashtam tenasyannam prasadhaya ||

verses.sa:
ब्राह्मण उवाच ।
इत्युक्ता तेन सा पत्री मृष्टमन्नं द्रिजस्य यत् ।
प्रसाधितवती तदू वै भर्त्तुर्वचनगौरवात् ॥
verses.rom:
brahmana uvacha |
ityukta tena sa patri mrishtamannam drijasya yat |
prasadhitavati tadu vai bhartturvachanagauravat ||

verses.sa:
तं भुक्तवन्तमिच्छातो मृष्टमन्नं महामुनिम् ।
निदाघः प्राह भूपाल! प्रश्रयावनतः स्थितः ॥
verses.rom:
tam bhuktavantamichchhato mrishtamannam mahamunim |
nidaghah praha bhupala! prashrayavanatah sthitah ||

verses.sa:
निदाघ उवाच ।
अपि ते परमा तृप्तिरुत्पन्ना तुष्टिरेव च ।
अपि ते मानसं खस्थमाहारेण कृतं द्रिज ॥
verses.rom:
nidagha uvacha |
api te parama triptirutpanna tushtireva cha |
api te manasam khasthamaharena kritam drija ||

verses.sa:
क्क निवासो भवान् विप्र ! क्क च गन्तु समुद्यतः ।
आगम्यते च भवता यतस्तज्व द्रिजोच्यताम् ॥
verses.rom:
kka nivaso bhavan vipra ! kka cha gantu samudyatah |
agamyate cha bhavata yatastajva drijochyatam ||

verses.sa:
ऋबुरुवाच ।
क्षुदू यस्य तस्य भुक्तेऽन्ने तृप्तिर्ब्राह्मण! जायते ।
न मे क्षु न्नाभवत् तृप्तिः कस्मान्मां परिपृच्छसि ॥
verses.rom:
riburuvacha |
kshudu yasya tasya bhukte'nne triptirbrahmana! jayate |
na me kshu nnabhavat triptih kasmanmam pariprichchhasi ||

verses.sa:
वह्निना पार्थिवे धातौ क्षयिते क्षु त्सनुद्भवः ।
भवत्यम्भांस च क्षीणो नृणां तृड़पि जायते ॥
verses.rom:
vahnina parthive dhatau kshayite kshu tsanudbhavah |
bhavatyambhamsa cha kshino nrinam trirapi jayate ||

verses.sa:
क्षुत्तृषौ देहधर्म्माख्ये न ममैते यतो द्रिज ।
ततः क्षु त्सम्भवाभावात् तृप्तिरस्त्येव मे सदा ॥
verses.rom:
kshuttrishau dehadharmmakhye na mamaite yato drija |
tatah kshu tsambhavabhavat triptirastyeva me sada ||

verses.sa:
मनसः स्वस्थता तुष्टिश्वित्तधर्म्माविमौ द्रिज ।
चेतसो यस्य तत् पृच्छ पुमानेबिर्न युज्यते ॥
verses.rom:
manasah svasthata tushtishvittadharmmavimau drija |
chetaso yasya tat prichchha pumanebirna yujyate ||

verses.sa:
क्व निवासस्तवेत्युक्तं क्व गन्तासि स यत् त्वया ।
कु तश्वागम्यते तत्र त्रितयेऽपि निबोध मे ॥
verses.rom:
kva nivasastavetyuktam kva gantasi sa yat tvaya |
ku tashvagamyate tatra tritaye'pi nibodha me ||

verses.sa:
पुमान् सर्व्वगतो व्यापा आकाशवदयं यतः ।
कुतः कुत्र क्व गन्तासीत्येतदप्यर्थवत् कथम् ॥
verses.rom:
puman sarvvagato vyapa akashavadayam yatah |
kutah kutra kva gantasityetadapyarthavat katham ||

verses.sa:
नाहं गन्ता न चागन्ता नैकदेशनिकेतनः ।
त्वं चान्येच न च त्वं त्वं नान्ये नैवाहमप्यहम् ॥
verses.rom:
naham ganta na chaganta naikadeshaniketanah |
tvam chanyecha na cha tvam tvam nanye naivahamapyaham ||

verses.sa:
मष्टं न मष्टमप्येषा जिज्ञासा मे कृता तव ।
किं वक्ष्यसीति तत्रापि श्रूयतां द्रिजसत्तम ॥
verses.rom:
mashtam na mashtamapyesha jijnasa me krita tava |
kim vakshyasiti tatrapi shruyatam drijasattama ||

verses.sa:
किमस्वादूथवा मृष्टं भुञ्जतोऽन्नं द्रिजोत्तम ।
मृष्टमेव यदामृष्टं तदैवोदू गकारकम् ॥
verses.rom:
kimasvaduthava mrishtam bhunjato'nnam drijottama |
mrishtameva yadamrishtam tadaivodu gakarakam ||

verses.sa:
अमृष्टं जायते मृष्टं मृष्टादुद्रिजते जनः ।
आदिमध्यावसानेषु किमन्नं रुचिकारकम् ॥
verses.rom:
amrishtam jayate mrishtam mrishtadudrijate janah |
adimadhyavasaneshu kimannam ruchikarakam ||

verses.sa:
मृन्मयं हि गृहं यदून्मृदा लिप्त स्थिरं भवेत् ।
पार्थिवोऽयं तथा देहः पार्थिवैः परमाणभिः ॥
verses.rom:
mrinmayam hi griham yadunmrida lipta sthiram bhavet |
parthivo'yam tatha dehah parthivaih paramanabhih ||

verses.sa:
यव-गोधूम-मुदूगादि घृतं तैलं पयो दधि ।
गुड फलादीनि तथा पार्थिवाः परमाणवः ॥
verses.rom:
yava-godhuma-mudugadi ghritam tailam payo dadhi |
guda phaladini tatha parthivah paramanavah ||

verses.sa:
तदेतदू भवता ज्ञात्वा मृष्टामृष्टविचारि यत् ।
तन्मनः समातालम्बि कार्य्यं साम्यं हि मुक्तय ॥
verses.rom:
tadetadu bhavata jnatva mrishtamrishtavichari yat |
tanmanah samatalambi karyyam samyam hi muktaya ||

verses.sa:
इतायाकर्ण्य वच्स्तस्य परमार्थाश्रितं नृफ!
प्रणिपत्य महाभागे निदाघो वाक्यमब्रवीत् ॥
verses.rom:
itayakarnya vachstasya paramarthashritam nripha!
pranipatya mahabhage nidagho vakyamabravit ||

verses.sa:
प्रसीद मद्धितार्थाय कथ्यतां यस्त्वमागतः ।
नष्टो मोहस्तवाकर्ण्य वचांस्येतानि मे द्रिज ॥
verses.rom:
prasida maddhitarthaya kathyatam yastvamagatah |
nashto mohastavakarnya vachamsyetani me drija ||

verses.sa:
ऋभुरस्मि तवाचार्य्यः प्रज्ञादानाय ते द्रिज!
इहागतोऽहं यास्यामि परमार्थस्तवोदितः ॥
verses.rom:
ribhurasmi tavacharyyah prajnadanaya te drija!
ihagato'ham yasyami paramarthastavoditah ||

verses.sa:
एवमेकमिदं विद्धि न भेदि सकलं जगत् ।
वासुदेवाभिधेयस्य स्वरूपं परमात्मनः ॥
verses.rom:
evamekamidam viddhi na bhedi sakalam jagat |
vasudevabhidheyasya svarupam paramatmanah ||

verses.sa:
तथेत्युक्त्वा निदाघेन प्रणिपातपुरः सरम् ।
पूजितः परया भतया इच्छातः प्रययावृभुः ॥
verses.rom:
tathetyuktva nidaghena pranipatapurah saram |
pujitah paraya bhataya ichchhatah prayayavribhuh ||

prose.en:
Parāçara said—Having heard those words the king became speechless and engaged in meditation and the Brahmin told a tale illustrating the principles of unity.

The Brahmin said—"Hear O great king what in the days of yore Ribhu said for the instruction of illustrious Nidagka. The great patriarch Brahmā had a son by Ribhu, who was by nature, O king, conversant with true wisdom. A son of Pulastya by name Nidagha became his disciple and (Ribhu) greatly delighted gave him various instructions. O lord of men, he being thus instructed, Ribhu did not doubt of his being fully confirmed in the doctrines of unity.

"The residence of Pulastya was at Viranagara, a big, beautiful city, situated on the banks of the river Devika. And there lived in a beautiful grove near this river, Nidagha, the disciple of Ribhu, acquainted with all devotional practices. After a thousand divine years Ribhu went to the city of Pulastya to see his pupil who stood at the gate after the completion of the sacrifice to Viswadevas. He was beheld by his pupil who came there specially to offer him Arghya, (the usual present) and led him into the house. And when his hands and feet were washed and he was seated Nidagha requested him respectfully to eat.

"Ribhu said—‘O foremost of Brahmins, tell me what food is there in your house? I do not like wretched food.'

"Nidagha said—‘There are cakes, of meal, rice, barley and pulse in my house. Eat, O reverend Sir, whatever pleases you best.'

"Ribhu:—O twice-born one, these are wretched viands. Give me sweet meats. Give me rice boiled with sugar, wheaten cakes and milk with curd and molasses.'

"Nidagha said—'O dame, quickly prepare whatever is most excellent and sweet in my house and satisfy him therewith.'

"Having been thus addressed the wife of Nidagha in consonance with her husband's behest prepared sweet food and placed it before the Brahmin. And, O king, he then, spoke humbly to the great Muni, who was delightedly eating the meal.

"Nidagha—‘Have you been greatly delighted with this meal, O twice-born one? Has your mind obtained contentment? Where is your residence, O Brahmin and where are you going? And tell me, whence art thou coming, O twice-born one?'

"Ribhu said:—‘O twice-born one, he, who has got appetite, is pleased with his meals. I have got no appetite and hence have got no satisfaction: why do you question me in vain? Hunger is created, when by fire the earthly element is dried; and thirst is produced when the moisture of the body is absorbed by internal heat. These are the the functions of the body, O twice-born one, not mine—I am satisfied with that by which they are removed. And pleasure and contentment are the faculties of the mind, O twice-born one; ask those men about it whose minds are affected by them. As regards your three other questions—Where I dwell, wither I go and whence I come, hear my reply.

"'Man goes everywhere and penetrates everywhere like the ether. Then is it rational to ask "Where is thy residence? Whence are you coming? And where will you go?" I am not coming from anywhere. I shall not go anywhere and I do not live in one place. Such is the case with you and other men. What people see of you is not real you; what people see of other men are not real they, and what people see of me is not real I. I made distinction between the sweetened and not sweetened food only to hear of your opinion about that: do thou hear my explanation about this, O twice-born one. Is there anything really sweet and not sweet to him who takes meals? That which is considered sweet is no longer so when it causes the sense of repletion, and that which is not sweet, becomes so when a man considers it as such. What food is there which is equally delightful from the first to the middle and last? As a house built of clay is strengthened by fresh plaster so this earthly body is maintained by earthly atoms. And barley, wheat, pulse, butter, oil, milk, curds, treacle, fruits and the like are made of earthly atoms. You have now understood what is sweet and what is not; do you so act that you may be impressed with the notion of identity which leads to final liberation.'

"Having heard those words explaining the true end of life, the illustrious Nidagha humbly bowed to him and said—'Be then propitiated with me, O twice-born one. Thou hast come here for my welfare. Tell me whence thou hast come? Hearing thy words the infatuation of my mind is removed'.

"Ribhu said:—'O twice-born one, I am thy preceptor Ribhu. I have come here to confer upon thee the true knowledge. Now I depart; for you have been acquainted with the true end of life. Consider again this universe to be one undivided nature of the supreme spirit Vāsudeva'.

"Having said 'so be it' Nidagha reverentially bowed to and worshipped him. And Ribhu too repaired to his wished-for quarter".

verses.sa:
ऋबुर्वर्षसहस्त्र तु समतीते नरेश्वर!
निदाघज्ञानदानाय तदेव नगरं ययौ ॥
verses.rom:
riburvarshasahastra tu samatite nareshvara!
nidaghajnanadanaya tadeva nagaram yayau ||

verses.sa:
नगरस्य वहिः सोऽथ निदाघं ददृशे मुनिः ।
महाबलपरीवारे पुरं विशति पार्थिवे ॥
verses.rom:
nagarasya vahih so'tha nidagham dadrishe munih |
mahabalaparivare puram vishati parthive ||

verses.sa:
दूरे स्थितं महाभागं जंनसम्मर्द्द वर्ज्जकम् ।
क्षु त्क्षामकण्ठमायान्तमराण्यात् ससमितुकुशम् ॥
verses.rom:
dure sthitam mahabhagam jamnasammardda varjjakam |
kshu tkshamakanthamayantamaranyat sasamitukusham ||

verses.sa:
दृष्वा निदाघं स ऋभुरुपगम्याभिवाद्य च ।
उवाच कस्मादेकान्ते स्थीयते भवता द्रिज ॥
verses.rom:
drishva nidagham sa ribhurupagamyabhivadya cha |
uvacha kasmadekante sthiyate bhavata drija ||

verses.sa:
बो विप्र ! जनसम्मर्द्दो महानेष महनिष जनिश्वरे ।
प्रविविक्षौ पुरं रम्यं तेनात्र स्थीयते मया ॥
verses.rom:
bo vipra ! janasammarddo mahanesha mahanisha janishvare |
pravivikshau puram ramyam tenatra sthiyate maya ||

verses.sa:
नराधिपोऽत्र कतमः कतमश्चेतरो जनः ।
कथ्यतां मे द्रिजश्वेष्ठ! त्वमभिज्ञो मतो मम ॥
verses.rom:
naradhipo'tra katamah katamashchetaro janah |
kathyatam me drijashveshtha! tvamabhijno mato mama ||

verses.sa:
योऽयं गजेन्द्रमुन्मत्तमद्रिश्वृङ्गसमुच्छिर्तम् ।
अधिरूढो नरेन्द्रोऽयं परलोकस्तथेतरः ॥
verses.rom:
yo'yam gajendramunmattamadrishvringasamuchchhirtam |
adhirudho narendro'yam paralokastathetarah ||

verses.sa:
एतौ हि गज-राजानौ युगपदू दशितौ मम ।
बवता न विशेषेण पृथकूचिह्नपिलक्षणौ ॥
verses.rom:
etau hi gaja-rajanau yugapadu dashitau mama |
bavata na visheshena prithakuchihnapilakshanau ||

verses.sa:
तत् कथ्यतां महाभाग ! विशेषो भवतानयोः ।
ज्ञातु मिच्छाम्यहं कोऽत्र गजः को वा नराधिपः ॥
verses.rom:
tat kathyatam mahabhaga ! vishesho bhavatanayoh |
jnatu michchhamyaham ko'tra gajah ko va naradhipah ||

verses.sa:
गजो योऽयमधो ब्रह्मन् ! उपर्य्यस्यैष भूपतिः ॥
वाह्म-वाहकसाबन्धं को न जानाति वै द्रिज ॥
verses.rom:
gajo yo'yamadho brahman ! uparyyasyaisha bhupatih ||
vahma-vahakasabandham ko na janati vai drija ||

verses.sa:
जानाम्यहं यथा ब्रह्म स्तथा मामवबोधम ।
अवःशह्दनिगद्य किं किञ्चोद्ध्व मभिधीयते ॥
verses.rom:
janamyaham yatha brahma statha mamavabodhama |
avahshahdanigadya kim kinchoddhva mabhidhiyate ||

verses.sa:
इत्युक्तः सहसारुह्म निदाघः प्राह त ऋबुम् ।
श्रूयतां कथयाम्येष यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि ॥
verses.rom:
ityuktah sahasaruhma nidaghah praha ta ribum |
shruyatam kathayamyesha yanmam tvam pariprichchhasi ||

verses.sa:
उपर्य्यहं यथा राजा त्वमधः कूञ्जरो यथा ।
अवबोधाय ते ब्रह्मन् ! दृष्टान्तो दसितो मया ॥
verses.rom:
uparyyaham yatha raja tvamadhah kunjaro yatha |
avabodhaya te brahman ! drishtanto dasito maya ||

verses.sa:
त्वं राजेव द्रिजश्वेष्ठ! स्थितोऽहं गजवद् यदि ।
तदेतत् त्वं समाचक्ष्व कतमस्त्वमहं तता ॥
verses.rom:
tvam rajeva drijashveshtha! sthito'ham gajavad yadi |
tadetat tvam samachakshva katamastvamaham tata ||

verses.sa:
इत्युक्तः सत्वरं तस्य प्रगृह्म चरणावुभौ ।
निदाघः प्राह भगवानाचार्य्यस्त्वमृबुध्रुर्वम् ॥
verses.rom:
ityuktah satvaram tasya pragrihma charanavubhau |
nidaghah praha bhagavanacharyyastvamribudhrurvam ||

verses.sa:
नान्यस्यादू तसंस्कारस्कृतं मानसं तथा ।
यथाचार्य्यस्य तन त्वां मन्ये प्राप्तमह गुरुम् ॥
verses.rom:
nanyasyadu tasamskaraskritam manasam tatha |
yathacharyyasya tana tvam manye praptamaha gurum ||

verses.sa:
तवोपदेशदानाय पूर्व्वशुश्रूषणादृतः ।
गुरुस्तेऽहमृभुर्नाम्रा निदाघ! समुपागतः ॥
verses.rom:
tavopadeshadanaya purvvashushrushanadritah |
guruste'hamribhurnamra nidagha! samupagatah ||

verses.sa:
तदेतदुपदिष्टं सङ्क्ष पेण महामते ।
परमार्थसारभूतं यददूतैमशेषतः ॥
verses.rom:
tadetadupadishtam sanksha pena mahamate |
paramarthasarabhutam yadadutaimasheshatah ||

verses.sa:
एवमुक्त्वा ययौ विद्रान् निदाघं स ऋबुर्गुरुः ।
नदाघोऽप्युपदेशीन तेनादूतैपरोऽभवत् ॥
verses.rom:
evamuktva yayau vidran nidagham sa riburguruh |
nadagho'pyupadeshina tenadutaiparo'bhavat ||

verses.sa:
सर्व्भूतान्यभेदेन ददृशे स तदान्मनः ।
यथा ब्रह्मपरो मुक्तिपवाप परमां द्रिज ॥
verses.rom:
sarvbhutanyabhedena dadrishe sa tadanmanah |
yatha brahmaparo muktipavapa paramam drija ||

verses.sa:
तथा त्वमपि धर्म्मज्ञ ! तुल्यात्मरिपुबान्धवः ।
भव सर्व्वगतं जानन्नात्मानमवनीपते ॥
verses.rom:
tatha tvamapi dharmmajna ! tulyatmaripubandhavah |
bhava sarvvagatam janannatmanamavanipate ||

verses.sa:
सितनीलादिभेदेन यथैकः दृश्यते नभः ।
भ्रान्तिदृष्टिभिरात्मापि तथैकं सन् पृथक् पृथक् ॥
verses.rom:
sitaniladibhedena yathaikah drishyate nabhah |
bhrantidrishtibhiratmapi tathaikam san prithak prithak ||

verses.sa:
एकः समस्तं यदिहास्ति किञ्चित्
तदच्युतो नास्ति परं ततोऽन्यत् ।
सोऽहं स च त्वं स च सर्व्वमेत- दात्मखरूपं त्यज भेदमोहम् ॥
verses.rom:
ekah samastam yadihasti kinchit
tadachyuto nasti param tato'nyat |
so'ham sa cha tvam sa cha sarvvameta- datmakharupam tyaja bhedamoham ||

verses.sa:
पराशर उवाच ।
इतीरितस्तेन स राजवर्य्य
स्तत्याज भेदं परमार्थदृष्टिः ।
स चापि जातिस्मरणाप्तबोध-
स्तत्रैव जन्मन्यपवर्गमाप ॥
verses.rom:
parashara uvacha |
itiritastena sa rajavaryya
statyaja bhedam paramarthadrishtih |
sa chapi jatismaranaptabodha-
statraiva janmanyapavargamapa ||

verses.sa:
इति भरतःनरेन्द्रसारवृत्तं
कथयति यश्व श्वृणोति भक्तियुक्तः ।
स विमलमतिरेति नात्ममोहं
भवति च संसरणेषु मुक्तियोग्यः ॥
verses.rom:
iti bharatahnarendrasaravrittam
kathayati yashva shvrinoti bhaktiyuktah |
sa vimalamatireti natmamoham
bhavati cha samsaraneshu muktiyogyah ||

verses.sa: ॥ द्रितीयांशः सम्पूर्णः ॥
verses.rom: || dritiyamshah sampurnah ||

prose.en:
"After the expiration of another thousand years Ribhu again repaired to that city for conferring knowledge upon him. The ascetic beheld Nidagha at the outside of the city when the king was about to enter it with a huge army and a host of relations. He saw his illustrious pupil standing at a distance avoiding the crowd—his throat was parched with hunger and thirst consequent upon carrying thicket fuel and holy grass. Beholding Nidagha and saluting him Ribhu said—'Why are you standing aloof, O twice-born one?'

"Nidagha said:—'There is a great rush of people for the lord of men is entering this huge and picturesque city; I am staying to avoid the crowd'.

"Ribhu said 'O foremost of twice-born one, who is the king amongst these? And who are his attendents. Methinks you know all these. Tell me'.

"Nidagha said:—'He, who is seated on the infuriated elephant, huge as a mountain, is the king: and all others are his attendents'.

"Ribhu said;—'You have simultaneously pointed out to me both the king and the elephant, but you have not particularly said, who is the king and which is the elephant. Therefore O illustrious one, tell me in particular, who is the king and which is the elephant; I am anxious to know it'.

"Nidagha said:—'That which is under is the elephant and one who is above is the king. Who is not aware, O twice-born one, of the relation between that which bears and that which is borne?'

"Ribhu said:—'Explain to me in the way in which I can understand it. What is meant by the word underneath and what is meant by the word above?'

"As soon as he had said this Nidagha jumped upon Ribhu and said—'Hear what you have asked of me. I am above like the king, you are underneath like the elephant. I show this example, O Brahman, for your better information'.

"Ribhu said—'O foremost of Brahmins, it seems that you are as if the king and I am the elephant and tell me now which of us two is you and which is I'.

"Ribhu having said this, Nidagha speedily got down and falling at his feet said, 'Sure thou art my saintly preceptor Ribhu. The mind of no other person is so much acquainted with the principles of unity as that of the mind of my preceptor. Therefore I know that thou art he'.

"Ribhu said:—'O Nidagha, I am your preceptor Ribhu. Pleased with the attention which you had shown to me before, I have come here to give you instructions O you gifted with a high mind. I have briefly described to you the divine truth, the essence of which is the none-quality of all'.

"Having said this the learned Ribhu went away. Nidagha, too by his instructions, was impressed with belief in unity. He began to observe all beings in no way distinct from him. And being devoted to Brahmā he obtained final liberation.

"Therefore, O king, O thou, conversant with duty, do thou, consider thyself as one with all beings, regarding equally friend or foe, the same sky looks apparently as white or blue so Soul, which is in reality one, appears diversified to erroneous vision. That, which exists in the universe, is one which is Achyuta. There is nothing distinct from Him. He is I. He is thou. He is all. This universe is His form. Give up therefore the misconceived notion of distinction".

Parāçara said:—The Brahmin having uttered this the king became cognizant of the true end of life. He renounced all idea of distinction and the Brahmin, who, on account of the recollection of former lives, had obtained perfect knowledge, now acquired liberation from future births.

He, who will reverentially hear this story of Bharata or narrate it, will have his mind illuminated and will not mistake the nature of individuality. And he who remembers it even shall be considered an object of reverence.

THE END OF PART II.
